title: Forest-Guided Semantic Transport for Label-Supervised Manifold Alignment
claim: A multi-stage procedure turns per-domain supervised structure into cross-domain correspondences and a joint embedding, without predefined anchors.
layout: 5 lettered stages, left-to-right, black module boxes on arrows, dashed cross-links
description: A horizontal five-stage flow labeled a to e. At far left, two curved manifold shapes, X_A on top and X_B on bottom, hold starred and circular points. A legend gives filled star and circle as class labels and a plus sign as a missing label. Black rounded 'Forest Geometry' boxes lead to green-shaded manifolds. Their arrows point into a white 'Intra-domain affinities W_A, W_B' box. A 'Semantic Projection' box leads to a green quarter-disc, the shared semantic space. A red arc on it marks the cross-domain semantic cost, and dashed curves link points from both domains to it. A 'HiRef' box leads to a transport plan T, drawn as lines joining the two manifolds. Next come the 'Cross-domain affinities W_AB, W_BA' box and a 'Joint Embedding' box. The last panel is a yellow square of mixed, aligned points. The eye starts at the top-left manifolds and follows the arrows rightward.
caption: Overview of FoSTA. (a) Given two (partially labeled) domains XA and XB, we compute semi-supervised, forest-derived affinities WA and WB to capture task-relevant neighborhood structure (Section 3.2). (b) We form class-wise semantic profiles and map samples from both domains to a shared, ℓ2-normalized semantic space, which defines a cross-domain semantic cost (Section 3.3). (c) Using this cost, HiRef estimates an efficient bijective transport plan T between domains (Section 3.3). (d) We propagate correspondences through T to build cross-domain affinities WAB and WBA consistent with the intra-domain graphs (Section 3.4). (e) Finally, we compute a joint low-dimensional embedding from the resulting block affinity matrix (Section 3.5).
abstract: Label-supervised manifold alignment bridges the gap between unsupervised and correspondence-based paradigms by leveraging shared label information to align multimodal datasets. However, existing methods either rely on label-independent intra-domain geometry or incorporate supervision primarily through the alignment objective, rather than directly constructing task-aware intra-domain affinities. To address this limitation, we introduce FoSTA (Forest-guided Semantic Transport Alignment), which learns supervised forest geometries independently within each domain and uses their shared class-semantic structure to infer cross-domain correspondences without predefined anchors. FoSTA extends RF-GAP affinities to partially labeled data and aligns the resulting semantic representations through scalable hierarchical transport. Extensive comparisons with established baselines demonstrate strong correspondence recovery and semantic structure preservation on synthetic and real-world benchmarks, including multimodal data integration and single-cell batch correction.
